title: Royal Garden, the Sunset and working for Joe Glazer
summary: In Chicago she moved from the Royal Garden to the Sunset with Louis; she describes Glazer, who managed sports figures, as kind and generous despite gangster ties.

story.theme_name: Gangsters, bootleggers and rough clubs of Prohibition
story.community_name: Gangsters, bootleggers and the Prohibition-era clubs

blocks.x: Probably --
If you haven't, I'm going to ask somebody. I know I worked and then I went over to the Royal Garden. And then from the Royal Garden I went to the Sunset. All this is in Chicago.
Sunset, Louis was working there?
That's right.
And Joe GlaSer's (PHONETIC) mother owned the building?
That's right. That's where I was. I
went over there with Louis. Of course, I got things with MR. Glazer's name and all on them. You know, I worked for Joe Glazer.
Do you remember Joe Glazer from that period?

Oh, the whole time, when he died, I was there. Sure, I stuck with him, because he was good to me. Mr. Glazer got me good work. And on top of getting me -- even if he never got it, he was a human. He had his faults, but he was a fine man and had a heart. He gave me $100.00 every year of my life for my church. Yes, he did. Mr. GlaSer, he gave me $100.00, and would ask me if that was enough. Yes, he did. And that was wonderful, you know.
When did you first meet him?
I met Mr. Glazer in Chicago.
At the Sunset?
Uh-huh.
He was managing some sports figures, wasn't he?
Yeah, he always managed sports figures.
Louis was the first performer?
That's right.
But he was involved with some gangsters during his life.
Always. At all times he was involved

with gangsters. But Mr. Glazer was -- he might have been involved with them, but he didn't do anything dirty. He was too nice a man, you know. He was a fine -- Mr. Glazer was such a lovely man. And you see, those gangsters get people in their clutches like that. But I haven't got a thing to say, because they were good to me. Because everytime I'd open my mouth singing a song, they'd give me a twenty or fifty dollar bill, or something. You know, they never bothered us. They never bothered us at all. And one of their main songs was "Melancholy Baby". Always "Melancholy Baby."
